- `src/catering/catering-states.mjs:35` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 1 (named exports only). `export default advanceOrder;` is a default export, and the only importer uses it as a default binding at `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:10` (`import advanceOrder, {canAmend, canCancel, newOrder} from './catering-states.mjs';`). The module breaks the repository export contract and the one-name-per-export convention used by every other module in the feature. Fix: change the definition at line 29 to `export const advanceOrder = (order, action, at) => {` (or add `export` to it), delete line 35, and change the import at `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:10` to a named import.

- `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:1` and `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:46` violate `src/AGENTS.md` rule 2. A rule module imports the Node built-in `node:crypto` (`createHash('sha256')`) to compute `digest`. Only store and platform modules may import built-ins. Fix: move the SHA-256 hex digest into a platform module (for example a new `src/platform/digest.mjs` exporting a function such as `sha256Hex(text)`), import it from `kitchen-manifest.mjs`, and remove the `node:crypto` import. No platform module currently provides hashing, so the platform module must be created.

- `src/catering/menu.mjs:11` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 3. `export const DIETARY_TAGS = Object.keys(DIETARY_LABELS);` exports a plain array that is not frozen. The array is exported directly and is shared with other modules (`src/catering/catering-statements.mjs:3,9` iterates it). Any importer can `push` into it and change the dietary tag set for every module. Fix: `export const DIETARY_TAGS = Object.freeze(Object.keys(DIETARY_LABELS));`.

- `src/catering/menu.mjs:37-40` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 4.1. `loadMenu` is a rule module, but it contains `try { items = JSON.parse(feed); } catch (error) { throw new Error('menu feed is not valid JSON', {cause: error}); }`. Rule modules must not catch errors. The caller `menuFor` in `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:16-21` already wraps any failure from `loadMenu` with the vendor-specific message and cause, so the catch in the rule module duplicates that handling in the wrong layer. Fix: move the JSON parse into the service (`menuFor`) or into a platform parser that is allowed to catch, and let `loadMenu` take already-parsed items and throw only on shape errors.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:34-35` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 4.2. `notifyVendor` replaces the caught error with `throw new Error(`vendor of order ${order.id} was not notified`, error);`. The second argument of `Error` is an options object, so the original error is ignored and is not preserved as `cause`. Contrast with `menuFor` at line 20, which correctly uses `{cause: error}`. Impact: the notifier failure (for example a transport error) is lost from the thrown error chain. Fix: `throw new Error(`vendor of order ${order.id} was not notified`, {cause: error});`.

- `src/catering/catering-store.mjs:34-40` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 4.3. The store swallows the write error with `.catch(() => undefined)` and returns that same chain: `this.#writes = this.#writes.then(...).catch(() => undefined); return this.#writes;`. The promise returned to the caller therefore resolves to `undefined` instead of rejecting with the original error, including the `request key is already used by order ...` error thrown inside the queued callback. The rule allows the catch only to keep the queue usable, while the caller's promise must still reject. Concrete consequence: `placeOrder` in `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:64` passes the result through `saveThenNotify` (`src/platform/records.mjs:7-10`), which calls `send(saved)` with `undefined`, so `placedNotice(undefined, menu)` in `src/catering/catering-notices.mjs:14-18` throws a `TypeError` instead of the intended duplicate-key error, and a failed save is reported as success to the caller. Fix: keep the queue usable with a separate chain and return the unmodified write promise, e.g. `const next = this.#writes.then(() => {...}); this.#writes = next.catch(() => undefined); return next;`.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:70-74` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 5 (exported functions must not mutate caller-supplied records). `addLine` makes a shallow copy `const amended = {...order};` (line 73) and then calls `amended.lines.push(prepareLine(line));`. The `lines` array is the same array object as `order.lines` of the record supplied by the caller or stored in the injected store, so the caller's record is changed. The mutation happens before `itemsFor(...)` at line 75, which can throw ("menu item ... is not offered" or a dietary mismatch), so a rejected amendment still leaves the stored record with the extra line. Fix: `const amended = {...order, lines: [...order.lines, prepareLine(line)]};` and compute the charge from `amended` as now.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:89-95` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 5. `postponeOrder` loads the record with `store.find(orderId)` (which in `src/catering/catering-store.mjs:21-22` returns the stored object itself) and then runs `Object.assign(order, {deliverAt, postponedAt: now()});` on it. The record is changed in the store before `checkDeliverySlot(...)` at line 95 validates the new slot. When the desk-closed, reservation-fit or room-clash check throws, the stored order keeps the rejected `deliverAt` and `postponedAt`, which corrupts later `deskDeliveries`, `clashesWith` and invoice data. Fix: build `const postponed = {...order, deliverAt, postponedAt: at};`, validate `postponed`, and save only the copy.

- `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:27` and `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:50-51` violate `src/AGENTS.md` rule 5. `inDeliveryOrder` is `(orders) => orders.sort(byDelivery)`, and the exported `kitchenManifests(orders, menus, period)` calls it on its caller-supplied `orders` argument (`const due = inDeliveryOrder(orders)`). `Array.prototype.sort` reorders the caller's array in place. The current caller `vendorManifests` (`src/catering/catering-service.mjs:152`) happens to pass a fresh array from `store.list`, which hides the defect, but the exported function changes its input. Fix: sort the filtered result only, e.g. `const due = orders.filter(...).sort(byDelivery);`, and delete `inDeliveryOrder`.

- `src/catering/catering-notices.mjs:54` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 6.1. `vendorNotice` is a rule module but reads the clock with `sentAt: Date.now(),`. Only service modules may read the current time, and only through their injected `now`. Impact: the vendor notice timestamp cannot be controlled in tests or by the caller, and it is not the same instant as the rest of the `placeOrder` call (`const at = now();` at `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:51`). Fix: pass the instant as a parameter, `vendorNotice(order, menu, sentAt)`, and call it from `notifyVendor` with the `at` value that `placeOrder` already holds, or pass the `at` value through `notifyVendor`.

- `src/catering/catering-pricing.mjs:35` and `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:111` violate `src/AGENTS.md` rules 6.2 and 6.3. `cancellationFee(order, context)` is a rule module that receives the whole service context and calls `context.now()` (`order.deliverAt - context.now() < CATERING.cancelCutoff`). Rule modules must receive instants as numbers, not a `now` function. In `cancelOrder` (line 111), `now()` is already called for `advanceOrder(order, 'cancel', now())`, and then `cancellationFee` calls the injected `now` a second time. One service call therefore reads the clock twice, and the canceled stamp and the fee decision can use different instants. Fix: in `cancelOrder` call `const at = now();` once, pass `at` to `advanceOrder` and to `cancellationFee(order, at)`, and change `cancellationFee` to `(order, at) => (order.deliverAt - at < CATERING.cancelCutoff ? order.charge.subtotal : 0)`.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:122-126` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 6.3 (a service function calls `now` at most once per call). `isUpcoming(now)` returns `(order) => canCancel(order) && order.deliverAt >= now()`, and `upcomingOrders` applies it with `.filter(isUpcoming(now))`. The injected clock is read once for every candidate order in the member's list, so the same call can compare orders against different instants. Fix: read `const at = now();` once in `upcomingOrders` and filter with `(order) => canCancel(order) && order.deliverAt >= at`.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:4` violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 7.2 (a feature module may import only rule modules of another feature, never its service or store modules). `import {isFrontDeskOpen} from '../schedules/front-desk-service.mjs';` imports the service module of the `schedules` feature, and `checkDeliverySlot` (line 40) calls it. Fix: move the pure opening-hours check into a platform module, allowed by rule 7.4 when the capability must be reused across features, and have `checkDeliverySlot` call that module, or have the caller inject the desk-open check. Importing `front-desk-service.mjs` directly is not allowed.

- Duplicated Code: `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:19-25` (`KITCHENS` and `kitchenFor`) re-implements the vendor routing already defined in `src/catering/vendors.mjs:9-12` (`vendorFor`: halal goes to `crescent`, headcount above 30 goes to `banquet`, otherwise `deli`). The manifest rule `order.headcount >= 31` is the same boundary written differently. Impact: when routing changes in `vendors.mjs` (for example the `LARGE_ORDER` threshold), kitchen manifests keep the old grouping, and orders are sent to one vendor while their manifest is generated under another. The manifest also labels kitchen keys as vendor ids (`manifestOf(vendorId, ...)` at line 55 and `menus[vendorId]`), so the coupling is implicit. Fix: group by the persisted `order.vendorId` (`Map.groupBy(due, (order) => order.vendorId)`), which `changeHeadcount` keeps consistent with routing (`src/catering/catering-service.mjs:84`), and delete `KITCHENS` and `kitchenFor`.

- Duplicated Code: `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:137` computes `const arrivesFrom = order.deliverAt - CATERING.deliveryLead;` for the desk list, duplicating the delivery window start defined once in `deliveryWindow` at `src/catering/catering-policy.mjs:22`. That window is already used for overlap checks (`clashesWith`, `fitsReservation`) and manifest selection (`src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:52`). Impact: a change to how the delivery window starts must be made in two places, and only one of them is covered by the window logic. Fix: `const arrivesFrom = deliveryWindow(order).startAt;` with `deliveryWindow` imported from `./catering-policy.mjs` (a same-feature rule module, which rule 7.1 allows).

- Middle Man: `src/catering/catering-time.mjs:1` (`export {DAY, addMinutes} from '../platform/time.mjs';`) only re-exports two platform values and adds no policy. Its importers are `src/catering/catering-policy.mjs:4` and `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:11`. Rule 7.1 lets feature modules import platform modules directly, so the indirection gives no benefit and makes the same platform function reachable under two paths. Fix: delete `catering-time.mjs` and import `addMinutes` and `DAY` from `../platform/time.mjs` in the two importers.

- Middle Man: `src/catering/menu.mjs:52` (`export const findMenuItem = (menu, id) => requireMenuItem(menu, id);`) is an alias of `requireMenuItem` on line 46 with the same behavior. The only use is `src/catering/catering-notices.mjs:2` and `:10`. Impact: two names exist for one lookup, and a reader cannot tell whether they differ in behavior. Fix: remove `findMenuItem` and use `requireMenuItem` in `catering-notices.mjs`.

- Speculative Generality: `src/catering/catering-statements.mjs:14-15` adds a `{withCanceled = false}` option to `vendorStatement` that changes counted orders. The only caller in the staged tree is `vendorStatements` at `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:145`, which never passes the option, so the `withCanceled` branch is dead code with no current requirement. Fix: remove the option and the `withCanceled` branch in `counted`, and add it when a caller needs it.

- Shotgun Surgery (course knowledge repeated across three modules): the set of courses is written in `src/catering/menu.mjs:13` (`COURSES`), in the `prepMinutes` switch at `src/catering/catering-policy.mjs:6-14` (with a `default` that throws), and in `SERVING_ORDER` at `src/catering/catering-notices.mjs:7`. Adding or renaming a course requires coordinated edits in all three files. A missed edit fails at a different point each time: `prepMinutes` throws only when a delivery is priced, and `SERVING_ORDER[...]` returns `undefined`, so the notice sort produces `NaN` and the order of items is undefined. Fix: define each course once in a persistent table in `menu.mjs` (for example `{breakfast: {servingOrder: 0, prepMinutes: 45}, ...}`), validate `course` against that table, and derive `prepMinutes` and the serving order from it.

- Divergent Change: `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:1-152` mixes the order lifecycle (`placeOrder`, `addLine`, `changeHeadcount`, `postponeOrder`, the `confirm`/`deliver`/`cancel` transitions and their notifications, lines 45-126) with read-side outputs (`deskDeliveries` at line 134, `memberInvoiceCharges` at line 148, `vendorStatements` at line 143, `vendorManifests` at line 150). The read-side functions change for reporting, invoicing and kitchen-format reasons and depend on different collaborators (`feeds` is needed only for manifests, `invoiceCharges` from `catering-pricing.mjs`, `kitchenManifests` from `kitchen-manifest.mjs`). Concrete burden: a change to a manifest or statement shape must touch the same file that owns the state machine and the order-placement checks, and the module's import graph (`schedules`, `reservations`, `billing`-related pricing, kitchen output) grows with every reporting feature. Fix: split the read-side functions into a separate `*-service.mjs` module, such as `catering-reporting-service.mjs`, that imports the same rule modules, and keep the lifecycle functions in `catering-service.mjs`.
